name: Bulgarian
family: Indo-European, Balto-Slavic, Slavic, South Slavic (eastern group)
variety: Standard Bulgarian (literary norm based on the north-eastern dialects, as spoken in Sofia)
sources: Ternes, Elmar & Vladimirova-Buhtz, Tatjana (1999). Bulgarian. In Handbook of the International Phonetic Association, 55-57. Cambridge University Press.
Scatton, Ernest A. (1984). A Reference Grammar of Modern Bulgarian. Columbus, OH: Slavica.
Scatton, Ernest A. (1993). Bulgarian. In B. Comrie & G. G. Corbett (eds.), The Slavonic Languages. London: Routledge.
Tilkov, Dimităr & Bojadžiev, Todor (1981). Bălgarska fonetika. Sofia: Nauka i izkustvo.
Pettersson, Thore & Wood, Sidney (1987). Vowel reduction in Bulgarian and its implications for theories of vowel production: a review of the problem. Folia Linguistica 21.
Wood, Sidney & Pettersson, Thore (1988). Vowel reduction in Bulgarian: the phonetic data and model experiments. Folia Linguistica 22.
Dimitrova, Snezhina (1997). Bulgarian speech rhythm: stress-timed or syllable-timed? Journal of the International Phonetic Association 27.
Misheva, Anastasia & Nikov, Michel (1998). Intonation in Bulgarian. In D. Hirst & A. Di Cristo (eds.), Intonation Systems. Cambridge University Press.
contrasts: six vowels, including the mid back unrounded (or central) /ɤ/ written ъ (сън [sɤn] 'dream' vs син [sin] 'son')

palatalised versus plain consonants, only before the back vowels /a ɤ ɔ u/ (бял [bʲaɫ], лято, коня); there is no contrast before front vowels, before consonants or word-finally. The soft consonants are also analysed as consonant plus /j/
voiced versus voiceless obstruents (neutralised word-finally and in clusters)
position of stress is lexically and grammatically contrastive (вълна: [ˈvɤɫnɐ] 'wool' vs [vɐɫˈna] 'wave'; ходи: [ˈxɔdi] 'walks' vs [xoˈdi] 'walked')
allophony: vowel reduction: unstressed /a/ and /ɤ/ merge as [ɐ]; unstressed /ɔ/ is raised towards /u/ ([o] to [ʊ]); /ɛ/ and /i/ are kept apart in the standard (raising of unstressed /ɛ/ is eastern and non-standard)

stressed endings spelled а, я are pronounced [ɤ], [jɤ] in the verb forms of the first person singular and third person plural and in the short masculine article (чета [t͡ʃɛˈtɤ], вървя [vɐrˈvʲɤ], четат [t͡ʃɛˈtɤt], мъжа [mɐˈʒɤ], града [ɡrɐˈdɤ])
word-final obstruents are devoiced (град [ɡrat], зъб [zɤp], мъж [mɤʃ])

obstruent clusters take the voicing of their last member (сватба [ˈsvadbɐ], изток [ˈistok], всичко [ˈfsit͡ʃko]), also between a preposition and its host (с брат [zbrat], от брата [od ˈbratɐ]); /v/ is devoiced but does not cause voicing (сват)
/l/ is velarised [ɫ] before back vowels, before consonants and word-finally, and clear [l] before front vowels; younger speakers often have a [w]-like realisation of [ɫ]
velars are fronted before front vowels; /x/ is velar
/n/ is [ŋ] before velars; /r/ is an alveolar trill or tap
щ is the sequence [ʃt]; я, ю after a vowel or word-initially are [ja], [ju]
phonotactics: soft consonants only before back vowels
no voiced obstruents before a pause
the sequences of ъ with r or l alternate in position according to the number of following consonants (връх, върхът; гръб, гърбът)
geminates occur only at morpheme boundaries (оттам, пролетта, странна)

stress.rule: Stress can fall on any syllable, may shift in inflection (град, градъ́т, градове́) and distinguishes some verb forms; it is not shown in ordinary spelling.
stress.cues: duration, intensity and vowel quality (unreduced vowel), with pitch in accented positions

rhythm.vowel_reduction: moderate: /a ɤ/ to [ɐ] and /ɔ/ towards [u] in unstressed syllables; no deletion
rhythm.notes: Traditionally called stress-timed because of vowel reduction; Dimitrova (1997) discusses the evidence, and rhythm measures place Bulgarian between the classic stress-timed and syllable-timed languages.

length.notes: No phonemic length. Stressed vowels are longer than unstressed ones. Double consonants at morpheme boundaries are pronounced long in careful speech.

intonation.declarative: rising accents on non-final stressed syllables, falling accent on the nuclear stressed syllable, low ending
intonation.yes_no_question: with the particle ли: high accent on the word before ли (the focus), then a fall to low; without ли (checking questions): rise on the last stressed syllable, staying high or rising to the end
intonation.wh_question: high accent on the question word, then a fall to low
intonation.continuation: rise on the last stressed syllable of the non-final phrase, high boundary
intonation.accent_shape: pre-nuclear accents rise through the stressed syllable with the peak late or in the next syllable; the nuclear accent in statements is a fall
intonation.notes: Based on Misheva & Nikov (1998) and the grammars.

tone.notes: No lexical tone or pitch accent.

problems: Stress is lexical, but eSpeak has only suffix rules and a list of about 2,800 words (bg_listx); other words get penultimate stress, so common words with final stress are wrong (вода, жена, планина, добре, момче, голям) and some with initial stress too (ябълка).
Vowel reduction depends on the stress, so every stress error also gives the wrong vowel qualities.
Stressed endings written а, я but pronounced [ɤ] (чета, вървя, четат, благодаря, the short article in мъжа, града) are read with [a] and without final stress.
Soft labials, к and р are coded as consonant plus a palatal glide phoneme; only soft д, т, н, з, с, г have their own phonemes.
Word-final и is lengthened to [iː] (бели, големи, български); Bulgarian has no long vowels.
Voicing assimilation is not applied across word boundaries except for the one-letter prepositions that are joined to the next word (от брата keeps [t]).
България is stressed on the last but one vowel ([bɐɫɡaˈria]) instead of [bɐɫˈɡarijɐ].
Only the default eSpeak tunes are used: wh-questions get the same fall-rise as yes-no questions, and ли-questions have no peak on the focused word.
good: final devoicing and regressive voicing assimilation (град, зъб, сватба, изток, всичко, сграда)
ъ as its own vowel, stressed and unstressed
reduction of unstressed /a/ and /ɤ/ to [ɐ]-like vowels and raising of unstressed /o/; for /a/ a weaker degree in the syllable before the stress
velarised [ɫ] versus clear [l] chosen by the following vowel
one-letter prepositions в, с joined to the following word with assimilation (с брат [zbrat])

notes: No formant, VOT or rhythm-metric values are given because I cannot quote published figures with confidence.
